react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome implicates three distinct but interconnected biological axes. The dominant signal is sterol-centric: cholesterol (KEGG:C00187) appears as a direct hit across RaMP multi-DB ORA (enriching REACT:R-HSA-1430728 'Metabolism' at FDR 1.34e-4 with fold-enrichment 35.8, and six additional Reactome sub-pathways), mummichog m/z-network analysis (MUMM:bile_acid_biosynthesis at p=0.022, MUMM:squalene_and_cholesterol_biosynthesis at p=0.049), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (KEGG:hsa00100 at p=0.099). The convergence of ORA fold-enrichment of 267–6755 across cholesterol-containing pathways with mummichog network connectivity (which tolerates annotation gaps) confirms that cholesterol-associated sterol metabolism is the primary affected system. The second axis is purine degradation, anchored by uric acid (KEGG:C00366 → CHEBI:17775), which hits in RaMP via REACT:R-HSA-5619115 'Disorders of transmembrane transporters' and REACT:R-HSA-5619047, and independently in mummichog's MUMM:purine_metabolism (p=0.049). The third axis is xenobiotic phase-I metabolism: coumarin (KEGI:C05851 → CHEBI:28794) enriches REACT:R-HSA-211945 'Phase I - Functionalization of compounds' (FDR 0.00266) and REACT:R-HSA-211859 'Biological oxidations', consistent with the benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide (C14853 → CHEBI:30614) also representing an electrophilic xenobiotic metabolite. The four metabolites that resolve to ChEBI IDs (coumarin, cholesterol, uric acid, 4-pyridoxic acid) were sufficient to drive the top RaMP enrichment even though two inputs (N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl C20319 → CHEBI:16580; methimazole C07190 → CHEBI:50673) could not be mapped to pathway members in the local database. The cross-paradigm consensus centres on cholesterol as a multi-pathway driver and uric acid as an independent purine-node driver, with xenobiotic phase-I metabolism as a secondary biological theme.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on cholesterol as the dominant sterol driver of this differential metabolome. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks REACT:R-HSA-1430728 Metabolism as the top hit (FDR=1.34e-4, fold-enrichment=35.8, n=4 metabolites: cholesterol, coumarin, uric acid, 4-pyridoxic acid), with REACT:R-HSA-211897 Cytochrome P450 - arranged by substrate type (FDR=0.0017) and REACT:R-HSA-211945 Phase I - Functionalization of compounds (FDR=0.0027) confirming xenobiotic metabolism as a coordinated axis. Mummichog m/z-network analysis independently yields MUMM:bile_acid_biosynthesis (p=0.021, overlap=3/3) and MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p=0.021, overlap=3/3) as its top two hits, both anchored by cholesterol and its biosynthetic intermediates. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently corroborates sterol involvement via KEGG:hsa00100 Steroid biosynthesis (p=0.099) and identifies a second axis centred on vitamin metabolism: KEGG:hsa00750 Vitamin B6 metabolism (p=0.022) is driven by 4-pyridoxic acid, and KEGG:hsa00230 Purine metabolism (p=0.165) is driven by uric acid. Cross-paradigm consensus identifies cholesterol as the primary multi-pathway driver linking three Mummichog hits (bile acid biosynthesis, C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism, Vitamin B6 metabolism) and two RaMP Reactome pathways (Cytochrome P450, Phase I Functionalization). Coumarin provides the direct xenobiotic bridge to Phase I metabolism in both RaMP and Mummichog. This sterol-centric, multi-axis signature is consistent with perturbation of both endogenous lipid homeostasis and exogenous compound clearance.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on cholesterol as the dominant sterol driver of this differential metabolome. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks REACT:R-HSA-1430728 Metabolism as the top hit (FDR=1.34e-4, fold-enrichment=35.8, n=4 metabolites: cholesterol, coumarin, uric acid, 4-pyridoxic acid), with REACT:R-HSA-211897 Cytochrome P450 - arranged by substrate type (FDR=0.0017) and REACT:R-HSA-211945 Phase I - Functionalization of compounds (FDR=0.0027) confirming xenobiotic metabolism as a coordinated axis. Mummichog m/z-network analysis independently yields MUMM:bile_acid_biosynthesis (p=0.021, overlap=3/3) and MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism (p=0.021, overlap=3/3) as its top two hits, both anchored by cholesterol and its biosynthetic intermediates. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently corroborates sterol involvement via KEGG:hsa00100 Steroid biosynthesis (p=0.099) and identifies a second axis centred on vitamin metabolism: KEGG:hsa00750 Vitamin B6 metabolism (p=0.022) is driven by 4-pyridoxic acid, and KEGG:hsa00230 Purine metabolism (p=0.165) is driven by uric acid. Cross-paradigm consensus identifies cholesterol as the primary multi-pathway driver linking three Mummichog hits (bile acid biosynthesis, C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism, Vitamin B6 metabolism) and two RaMP Reactome pathways (Cytochrome P450, Phase I Functionalization). Coumarin provides the direct xenobiotic bridge to Phase I metabolism in both RaMP and Mummichog. This sterol-centric, multi-axis signature is consistent with perturbation of both endogenous lipid homeostasis and exogenous compound clearance.
